mail.description: one letter's envelope, sent or received

to.description: the address it is written to — absent when `deliver.to` names the recipient as an entity instead

at.description: when it was written, or when it arrived

target.description: the entity this letter is about — any entity at all, so correspondence hangs off the thing it concerns

message_id.description: the Message-ID other mail systems know this letter by — written from what arrived, and what a reply threads on

verified.description: whether the sending domain signed for this letter (DKIM) — false is recorded, never dropped: a letter nobody signed for is still a letter, and the reader is the one who decides what to trust

in_reply_to.description: the Message-ID this letter answers, exactly as the header wrote it — what arrives before `reply_to` can name an entity, and all a reply to a letter nobody kept ever has

sent_id.description: the id the sending service returned when it accepted this letter — written by whoever sent it, and what a delivery report is looked up by

email.description: an address, as an entity — what a person is reachable at

deliver.description: who a letter is for, as an entity in your graph

to.description: the recipient — their address is looked up when the letter goes out

delivered.description: the letter left: half of the outcome pair

via.description: how it went — the id the sender returned, or the address it went to

bounced.description: the letter did not leave: the other half

reason.description: what went wrong, as the sender reported it

notified.description: a recipient was told about something

inbox_list.title: What is waiting for me
inbox_list.description: Every letter addressed to one reader and not yet archived, newest first — routed to them, written to them, or delivered to an address they have. `●` is unread, `·` read, `×` archived. Archiving is the only thing that takes a letter out, so an empty list is one they emptied.

who.description: whose inbox to read (default: whoever is asking)

all.description: the archived ones too — the way back to anything hidden

inbox_archive.title: Hide it until it needs me again
inbox_archive.description: Take one item out of the inbox. Nothing is deleted and no history is lost — `inbox list --all` shows it again, and a later letter on the same thread arrives as its own item.

item.description: the item to hide — any entity an inbox can carry

mail_show.title: Read the letter
mail_show.description: One letter whole — its envelope, its words, and the rest of its thread with this one marked. Reading IS the mark: it stamps the letter opened, which is why this writes where `graph_show` only reads.

mail_reply.title: Answer it
mail_reply.description: Write a reply threaded on one letter and request that it be sent. It is addressed to the FAR side — an arrival's author, or your own sent letter's recipient — from the address the original used, with the subject prefixed `Re:`. Answering an arrival archives it: a thread you have replied to is not one waiting on you. The configured sender carries it; a graph that names none records the letter and never sends it.

mail_send.title: Write a letter
mail_send.description: Create a letter and request that it be sent. `to` is an address, or the id of somebody in this graph; an address nobody here has becomes an `email` entity, so the address book grows by use. `from` defaults to the address whoever is asking has. The configured sender carries it and writes `delivered` or `bounced` back onto the letter.

to.description: an address, or the id of whoever it is for

from.description: the address it is from (default: the caller's own)

about.description: the entity this letter is about, so the correspondence hangs off it

mail_check.title: Check the mail
mail_check.description: Check that every letter that arrived carries a sender. A letter that has a Message-ID but no `from` is one nobody can ever answer — the reply has no address to go to.
